summary.headline: Lords Chloro Q2 FY27 total income rose about 14% YoY to INR115 crore on higher caustic volumes, despite weaker caustic realisations.
summary.overview: Management said H1 FY27 performance was similar to H1 FY26 despite significantly lower caustic soda realisations, credited to cost efficiencies from renewable power. Q2 FY27 total income was about INR115 crore versus about INR100 crore in Q2 FY26, with caustic lye sales of about 23,300 tonnes versus 21,000 tonnes. Q2 profitability fell quarter-on-quarter, which management attributed mainly to a INR6 crore rise in raw material cost (paraffin oil, sulphuric acid) and higher employee incentives. A 21 MW DC solar captive plus BESS was commissioned in September, taking renewable share to about 40% of energy, and the INR315 crore capex plan is due for completion by July 2027.

segments.name: Caustic soda (lye)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume about 23,300 tonnes, the highest quarterly lye sales cited, with volume growth over 9% YoY per management. Realisations fell sharply in Q1 and were said to have improved since the prior quarter.

segments.name: Chlorinated paraffin wax (CPW)
segments.commentary: Volumes up over 40% YoY; management said CPW is about 20-25% of income. Margins are volatile, ranging from 0% to 20% depending on paraffin oil and CPW prices.

guidance_outlook: FY28 revenue expected to be at least INR550 crore, rising to INR550-600 crore with the current capex plan, with about nine months of sales from the new plant.
Caustic soda capacity to rise from about 300 tonnes per day to about 360 tonnes per day by July 2027 (March-July commissioning window).
Post-July 2027, management expects at least INR15-20 crore quarterly EBITDA and about INR80 crore annual free cash flow.
Target of about 70-80% renewable energy share within 2-3 years, contingent on Rajasthan policy allowing 2x contract demand in renewables.
Management expects the raw material cost headwind to ease and power costs to fall further.
capex_capacity: Total capex plan INR315 crore: about INR150 crore completed in FY26, remaining about INR165 crore to be completed by July 2027 at the latest.
Renewable capacity raised to 47 MW DC (captive plus group captive) after 21 MW DC solar with BESS was sanctioned and commissioned in September 2026; about 40% of power now renewable.
Power cost per unit: grid about INR8.3, captive solar about INR2, group captive about INR4.50.
Caustic soda: a further large electrolyser of about 120-140 tonnes would take capacity to about 500 tonnes including flakes, at an estimated INR140-150 crore; timeline not committed.
Battery storage (BESS) is about 1.45 MW, which management said is mandated by law; the 10 MW wind-solar hybrid project is already generating power.
demand_pricing: Caustic soda priced at import-parity: Gujarat/port about INR32,000-33,000 per tonne, Alwar/North about INR36,000-37,000 per tonne; company targets Gujarat price plus INR4,000-5,000.
Chlorine realisations in Alwar improved to between negative INR1,000 and zero per tonne from negative INR4,000-4,500; Gujarat at about negative INR2,000.

India net caustic soda exports declined; new capacity from Reliance (about 6 to 8 million tonnes) and Adani (to about 10 million tonnes) expected, with management citing about 5% annual demand growth.
Flakes (100% caustic) planned for about 100 tonnes of the 360 tonnes per day, enabling truck-based distribution and possible exports.
Captive chlorine: about 150 tonnes sold in open market and 100 tonnes consumed internally, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company see its scale and product mix evolving over the next 5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue of at least INR550 crore next year, and sees CPW at 20-25% of income, with a move into specialty chemicals funded by about INR80 crore annual free cash flow from July 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Are acquisitions or partnerships being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is looking at expansion and acquisitions, possibly in specialty chemicals, and that INR80 crore free cash flow could support a INR200 crore loan to acquire a INR250-300 crore company; no target is identified yet.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the QoQ profit decline despite lower power cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material cost rose about INR6 crore QoQ due to paraffin oil and sulphuric acid price spikes linked to the US-Iran conflict, and variable incentives are paid half-yearly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renewable share target and status of the wind-solar hybrid project?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of energy is now renewable since early October; target is 70-80% within 2-3 years. The 10 MW wind-solar hybrid is already generating and included in results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to move caustic soda from 300 to 500 tonnes and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity goes to 360 tonnes by July 2027; the next step to 500 tonnes needs INR140-150 crore with no committed timeline, and funding options are internal accruals, debt and promoter equity (promoters hold about 74%).

qa_highlights.question: What remuneration changes were made?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the managerial remuneration cap was reduced from 4-6% to 4% of profits for the next financial year, approved by the board and shareholders; the exact policy was not shared on the call.

risks_watch: Caustic soda realisations remain volatile; Q1 FY27 was described as the weakest in a long time, and the Q2 margin squeeze came from raw material costs.
CPW margins swing between 0% and 20% with paraffin oil and CPW prices.
Timeline risk on capex completion (July 2027) and on the 500-tonne caustic expansion, which has no committed date.
New Reliance and Adani capacity could pressure caustic prices and India's export position.

Promoter remuneration cut to 4% of profits; exact policy not disclosed on the call. Several figures were stated approximately and some ECU and quarterly realisation data were deferred to a follow-up with the CFO.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost efficiency and long-term growth, but cautious and deferential on specifics: it deferred ECU, remuneration policy and timelines to later follow-ups. It acknowledged Q2 as a tough quarter driven by raw material costs.
key_quotes: That's primarily because of the improvement in our cost efficiencies.
